parsed_response.reasoning: The diff wraps hubspot's token refresh in refreshOAuthTokens (CalendarService.ts:~174-186). When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, refreshOAuthTokens (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts) does `const response = await fetch(...); return response;` — a raw fetch Response — while the else branch returns the hubspotClient token object. The caller types the result as HubspotToken and immediately reads fields like refresh/expires_in, so in sync mode it reads a Response object instead of a token; no refresh_token data is present, errors are not surfaced, and the expired credential is persisted. This is a real type-confusion defect introduced by the diff (only affects the opt-in sync path, hence slightly reduced confidence).

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts, the code wraps the token refresh call with refreshOAuthTokens(). The refreshOAuthTokens function (in packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts) returns either a fetch Response object (when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true) or the result of refreshFunction(). The original HubSpot code expected hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken() to return a HubspotToken object directly. When the sync endpoint is used, it returns a fetch Response instead, which would not have the expected token properties (access_token, refresh_token, etc.), causing the subsequent code that uses hubspotRefreshToken to fail or behave incorrectly.
